2 0 token introspection endpoint and accepts the token while the response reports it as active the introspection endpoint reports a token as inactive once its exp expiration time has passed so on this path the active flag is what enforces token expiry introspection results are cached by default introspectioncacheenabled true introspectioncachettl 60 seconds and both cache implementations shipped with the component concurrentmaptokencache and caffeinetokencache expired an entry a fixed time after it was inserted without bounding that lifetime by the exp claim that the cached response already permissions the expired token had carried although rfc 7662 which defines token introspection states that a response containing exp must not be cached beyond that time the access token is supplied by the caller with each request typically as a bearer token in the authorization header so a caller holding a token that was valid moments earlier could keep using it after it expired for as long as the cached entry lived the window is bounded by introspectioncachettl which is 60 seconds by default and 300 to 600 seconds where the documentation s recommendation for internal services was followed and
